blockPrompts.text:
Block type: text.
Output mode after FIX: SPAN-EDIT (`old_substring => new_substring`, one change per line, with enough surrounding words to match uniquely).

Check characters, digits, punctuation, case, homoglyphs, and reading order.
Preserve original language, author spelling, and paragraph breaks.
Do not reflow lines or normalize typography when equivalent.
blockPrompts.title:
Block type: title or heading.
Output mode after FIX: SPAN-EDIT (`old_substring => new_substring`, one change per line).

Check letters, digits, case (including ALL CAPS vs Title Case), punctuation, and section numbers.
Preserve original language, spelling, and heading markers.
Do not merge, split, or reorder words when equivalent.
blockPrompts.abstract:
Block type: abstract or summary.
Output mode after FIX: SPAN-EDIT (`old_substring => new_substring`, one change per line, with unique surrounding context).

Check words, numbers, statistical values, symbols, punctuation, case, and reading order.
Preserve original language, spelling, and paragraph structure.
Do not summarize, rewrite, or reflow.
blockPrompts.list:
Block type: list.
Output mode after FIX: SPAN-EDIT (`old_substring => new_substring`, one change per line; include the item marker in `old_substring` when fixing a marker).

Check item markers (bullets, numbers, letters, Roman numerals, dashes), indentation, item text, punctuation, and order.
Preserve original language, spelling, and list hierarchy.
Do not renumber or merge/split items when equivalent.
blockPrompts.code:
Block type: source code.
Output mode after FIX: SPAN-EDIT (`old_substring => new_substring`, one change per line; include full line or line prefix for uniqueness).

WHITESPACE OVERRIDE: in `code`, indentation, space counts, quotes (" vs ' vs `), and line breaks are NEVER equivalent when syntactically significant.
Check identifiers, keywords, operators, strings, numbers, brackets, semicolons, and comments.
 pay special attention to `0` vs `O`, `1` vs `l` vs `I`, `_` vs space, and `-` vs `--`.
Do not fix bugs, reformat, or complete partial code.

Return REVIEW whenever any differing character on the stamp is smudged, overlapping signature ink, or ambiguous.

Never normalize date formats, phone numbers, or numeric separators.
blockPrompts.table:
Block type: table.
Output mode after FIX: FULL-BLOCK with mandatory `EDITS:` audit trail.

Format when returning FIX:
FIX
<complete corrected table in the SAME serialization as the candidate: HTML if candidate is HTML, Markdown pipe table if candidate is Markdown; convert to HTML only if candidate markup is broken or cannot represent required rowspan/colspan>
EDITS:
r{row}c{col}: old_value => new_value
(1-based row and column indices; use `structure: description` for row/colspan or row/column count fixes)

Compare cells by row and column position. Check every number, decimal separator, sign, arrow, label, superscript/footnote marker, and unit.
Check row order, column order, empty cells, rowspan, and colspan.
Do not calculate, round, sort, fill blank cells, or infer missing values.
Do not restyle valid markup.
blockPrompts.equation:
Block type: mathematical formula.
Output mode after FIX: FULL-BLOCK with mandatory `EDITS:` audit trail.

Format when returning FIX:
FIX
<complete corrected LaTeX formula preserving candidate delimiters>
EDITS:
old_fragment => new_fragment

Check every symbol, Greek letter, subscript, superscript, fraction, radical, sum/integral limit, operator, relation, matrix entry, bracket, accent/hat/bar/vec, and equation number (e.g. `(1.2a)`).
Preserve visible bold/upright distinctions (`\mathbf`, `\mathrm` vs italic).
Treat as equivalent: whitespace, `\left/\right` vs bare delimiters when unambiguous, `\frac` vs `\dfrac`, `\to` vs `\rightarrow`, `\le` vs `\leq`, `\ge` vs `\geq`.
Do not simplify, factor, expand, evaluate, or replace with a familiar identity.

launch.name: spec-type
launch.description: Speculative decoding with the MTP head shipped inside the -MTP GGUF weights.

launch.name: spec-draft-n-max
launch.description: Draft tokens per step; 4 is what the MTP head was trained for.

launch.name: special
launch.description: Emit special tokens in the server output (strip <|im_end|> in parser).

launch.name: temp
launch.description: Server-side default sampling temperature; greedy decoding for transcription.

launch.name: parallel
launch.description: A single decoding slot; MTP drafting is single-stream.

launch.name: no-warmup
launch.description: Skip the warmup run at model load (faster start, slower first request).

launch.name: jinja
launch.description: Use the chat template from the GGUF metadata.

launch.name: reasoning-budget
launch.description: Budget for thinking tokens; 0 disables reasoning so the reply is the verdict only.

launch.name: flash-attn
launch.description: Flash attention kernels; required for the vision stack.

launch.name: image-min-tokens
launch.description: Vision budget floor; llama.cpp warns that Qwen-VL needs at least 1024 image tokens for grounding tasks.

request.name: repeat_penalty
request.description: Penalty for repeating tokens; 1.0 disables it (critical for numbers and tables).

request.name: presence_penalty
request.description: Penalty for tokens already present in the prompt; 0 disables it.

request.name: frequency_penalty
request.description: Penalty proportional to token frequency; 0 disables it.

request.name: stream
request.description: Stream tokens as they arrive; false gives the parser one complete response.

request.name: cache_prompt
request.description: Reuse the prompt cache; false avoids the recurring-state position warnings Qwen3.5 logs when blocks share a prefix.

request.name: stop
request.description: Stop sequences to prevent runaway generation after verdict.
